name: captive_portal
title: A hotel sign-in page
description: Something intercepts every request at once. Every layer looks broken, and blaming the internet provider would be confidently wrong.

card.title: The far end is slow to answer
card.summary: Your router and the path out to the internet both look normal, but the services we test are taking 79 ms to send their first byte, about 60 ms more than the network itself explains.
remediation: Check whether other sites are fine; if they are, the problem is at the far end and not with your connection.
Check the service's own status page.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

card.title: Name lookups are failing
card.summary: 50% of name lookups are failing. DNS is the internet's phone book, so when it stops answering, sites fail to load even though the connection itself is up.
remediation: Flush the DNS cache on this device.
Try a different DNS resolver in your network settings.
Power cycle your router: unplug it for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.

evidence.label: fraction of DNS probes that failed or timed out

card.title: A sign-in page is intercepting this network
card.summary: Something on this network is answering for every address, which is what a hotel or cafe sign-in page does. Nothing else can be measured until you sign in.
remediation: Open a browser and complete the network sign-in page.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

evidence.label: fraction of DNS probes that failed or timed out
